{"description":"PLANNED, 2026-09-12 (increment 437). Three parts, one capability because they are useless apart.

THE LEDGER. Every tool call the server answers appends one line to `<graph-path>.usage.jsonl` beside the design's store — the sidecar convention `.meta.json`, `.server.json` and `.client.json` already follow. A line carries: the moment, the tool name, the outcome class (`ok`, `refused`, `error`), the refusal class when refused (near_match, missing_argument, unknown_argument, unresolved_reference, refused, other — derived from a fixed table of the server's own phrasings, so the message itself is never stored), the duration, the harness name and version from the handshake, the seat, and for `get_skill` alone the skill name (reflow2's vocabulary, not the user's). NEVER an argument, a node id, a statement, or a message. An in-memory design writes nothing; a write that fails never fails the call (the handshake's own rule).

THE REPORT. A read tool, `usage_report`, renders the ledger since the previous report's marker or since a date the caller names: calls by tool, the served tools never called in the window, refusals by class and by tool, skills fetched, harnesses seen, the window's bounds — plus what the server knows without asking: reflow2's version, OS and architecture, the negotiated protocol revision, the design's node count. It appends a marker line so the next report starts after it, which is what makes "since last time" real. The unit is the PROJECT, not the session: the ledger is written by every session that ever served this design, from any harness.

THE SKILL. `feedback`, served with the `/feedback` shortcut and a command file in the kit for every harness. It calls the tool, adds the model as the agent's self-report labelled as such (the one field no harness sends over the protocol), invites one line of disposition per refusal row (guard working / real defect / unexplained) and any reproduction, appends the whole to the project's own `reflow2_feedback.md`, and shows it to the person. It never files or sends anything: typing the command is consent to compose, not to send.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SEE: anything outside reflow2's own tool calls. A shell pipe, a git error, a red CI — `report-friction` remains the form for those, with the agent as witness.","name":"/feedback renders a tally the server kept — tools used, refusals by class, harness and version metadata — for the person to carry","provenance":"authored","status":"verified","tier":"operational"}
